title: Although It Is True That: Si Bien and Remittances

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* "although it is true that" from B2 Unit 8. It is formal, it takes the indicative, and the clause that follows says what matters more. Money that migrants send home is a topic with two sides, so it suits this pattern.

items.spanish: Si bien las remesas ayudan a muchas familias, no sustituyen la inversión pública.
items.english: Although remittances help many families, they do not replace public investment.

items.spanish: Las remesas, si bien llegan por celular, no siempre llegan rápido.
items.english: Remittances, although they arrive by mobile phone, do not always arrive quickly.

items.spanish: Si bien muchos profesionales emigran, algunos vuelven con nuevas ideas.
items.english: Although many professionals emigrate, some come back with new ideas.

items.spanish: Si bien la familia vive lejos, mantiene el contacto todos los días.
items.english: Although the family lives far away, it keeps in touch every day.

sections.content: Choose by register: *aunque* in everyday speech, *si bien* in a report or an essay. Both take the indicative for a fact, and *si bien* never takes *que*.
